stories.headline: DOJ defends Trump’s White House media ban: access is a “privilege,” not a right
stories.summary: The Justice Department told a federal judge that President Trump can bar CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from White House grounds, casting hard-pass access as a privilege tied to national security and professional conduct. Court papers cite alleged disclosures about East Wing security work, a leak probe, and ballroom funding details. A hearing is set for Wednesday as the outlets argue the ban violates the First Amendment.

stories.headline: ICE’s “Operation Rotten Apple” nets more than 2,000 arrests across New York
stories.summary: Federal immigration officers reported more than 2,000 arrests statewide in a New York crackdown officials branded Operation Rotten Apple, highlighting child rapists, murderers, and other serious offenders among those taken into custody. DHS leaders framed the sweep as overdue enforcement against criminal noncitizens. Local critics and later reporting stressed that many citywide arrestees lacked prior criminal records, keeping the assimilation and sanctuary debate hot through September.

stories.headline: Matt Walsh: diesel spiral and Ukraine refinery strikes could fuel a deeper energy crisis
stories.summary: In a September 21 essay tied to his show, Matt Walsh argues that conventional “Iran war = high gas” framing understates a diesel and refining shock as Ukraine hits Russian fuel infrastructure. He relays a former White House official’s hard-line warning and calls for an immediate end to U.S. tolerance of those strikes. A follow-up episode on September 22 also highlighted alleged PPP-loan funding linked to the Haitian president’s assassination.

stories.headline: Erika Kirk faces online pile-on after fishing-trip photos shared after Charlie’s anniversary
stories.summary: On September 23, Erika Kirk drew fresh X criticism over Instagram photos from a mountain fishing trip she described as a place Charlie had wanted to visit with their children. A political account questioned the identity of people pictured without providing evidence. The flare-up lands weeks after polarized reactions to her “until Heaven” anniversary tribute and continued scrutiny of her leadership of Turning Point USA.

stories.headline: Elon Musk calls Xi a “great leader” and praises Tesla’s Shanghai Gigafactory on Chinese state TV
stories.summary: In a September 23 interview with Chinese state broadcaster CCTV, Elon Musk praised President Xi Jinping as a great leader and highlighted China’s infrastructure buildout and rising living standards. He called Tesla’s Shanghai plant a “gem” and credited local talent for its success. Musk also encouraged travelers to visit Beijing, Shanghai, and Xi’an — comments sure to ripple through U.S. politics and tech circles.

stories.headline: xAI launches Grok 4.7 for coding, agents, and knowledge work — now in GitHub Copilot
stories.summary: xAI introduced Grok 4.7 around September 21 as a longer-horizon model aimed at coding, agent workflows, and serious knowledge work. The company posted pricing and availability across the xAI API, Grok Build, and Cursor, with GitHub confirming Copilot access the same week. This is capability news — not hustle-funnel spam — and fits genuine AI tooling interest.

stories.headline: iPhone Duo countdown: 15 features to know before October pre-orders
stories.summary: Apple’s first foldable iPhone Duo is racing toward October 16 pre-orders and an October 23 launch after the September 9 “Surprise and Shine” event. MacRumors rounds up hinge design, dual displays, A20 Pro silicon, dual-battery behavior, IP68 sealing, and the $1,999 starting price. Separately, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12 with the new Health Sensing System began shipping September 18.

stories.headline: LEGO Ideas Downton Abbey: 4,711-piece Highclere Castle set arrives in October
stories.summary: On September 10 the LEGO Group unveiled LEGO Ideas Downton Abbey (21373), a 4,711-piece adult set recreating Highclere Castle with upstairs and downstairs rooms and 13 minifigures. Insiders early access begins October 1, with general release October 4 at $349.99. It headlines a busy September slate that already brought Bikini Bottom, the Enterprise bridge, and Batman Returns Batmobile to shelves.

stories.headline: Canon EOS R8 Mark II: lightweight full-frame with stronger IBIS and film-tone looks
stories.summary: Canon’s mid-September launch of the EOS R8 Mark II targets travelers and creators who want full-frame quality without bulk. The 24.2MP body adds improved 5-axis in-body stabilization plus NegativeFilmtone and PositiveFilmtone color profiles aimed at stills and video storytelling. New EOS R-system accessories round out the announcement for photographers stepping up from APS-C or older RF bodies.

stories.headline: Insta360 Luna Pro goes global: Leica-tuned gimbal camera with 8K and 4K vertical video
stories.summary: Insta360’s Luna Pro, co-engineered with Leica, expanded to global markets in September with a 1-inch sensor, 8K capture, and strong overlap with the higher-end Luna Ultra feature set. PetaPixel notes 4K vertical video aimed at everyday vlogging and social workflows. A companion firmware update for Luna Ultra also added Stage Mode and deeper in-camera zoom for live performances.

stories.headline: Harley-Davidson and Realtree drop second limited-edition camo apparel collection
stories.summary: On September 16 Harley-Davidson and Realtree released their second limited collaboration of apparel and accessories built for riders who also live outdoors. The drop expands into cargo pants, reversible vests, work shirts, hoodies, and caps using Realtree APG patterns with H-D branding. Pieces are available now at h-d.com/realtree and participating U.S. dealerships.

stories.headline: 2027 Jeep Wrangler JL-2A: retro tribute to the original Willys CJ-2A
stories.summary: Jeep’s September reveal of the Wrangler JL-2A — part of the Twelve 4 Twelve special-edition run — tips its hat to the 1945 Willys CJ-2A with retro styling on a Rubicon foundation. Orders are expected to open in October for a limited run aimed at heritage buyers. Separately, Jeep and Harley-Davidson kept their European community partnership visible at Bike Week earlier this month.

stories.headline: GM technical bulletin targets valvetrain tick: rocker arms and lash adjusters under scrutiny
stories.summary: General Motors’ PIP6101-series bulletins address a top-end ticking noise on recent Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC models, tracing it to debris affecting hydraulic valve lash adjusters. Dealers may inspect and replace all 16 rocker arms and adjusters when defects are found — a service fix, not a formal recall with owner mailings. For owners chasing a persistent “keep ticking” sound, this remains the live shop guidance in 2026.

stories.headline: Five Finger Death Punch drops “Legacy” music video as physical albums hit shelves
stories.summary: Five Finger Death Punch premiered the official video for the title track of their album Legacy in mid-September as physical editions arrived in stores. The clip keeps the band’s arena-metal punch front and center for longtime fans of 2000s hard rock and modern metal radio. Coverage from Blabbermouth and rock outlets framed the release as a full-cycle album moment, not just a streaming single drop.

stories.headline: Jets reshuffle roster: Onyemata to IR, Reeder and others elevated after Packers loss
stories.summary: On September 22 the Jets executed a wave of roster moves, placing David Onyemata, Arian Smith, and Marcelino McCrary-Ball on injured reserve while elevating Troy Reeder and others to the active roster. Practice-squad additions included Will Levis among several new names as the team digests an overtime loss to Green Bay. Coach Aaron Glenn continues to stress defensive yardage strength while looking ahead to Detroit.

stories.headline: Penguins’ center depth already tested as Kindel and Lizotte deal with injuries
stories.summary: Pittsburgh’s preseason opened with a 4–1 win over Buffalo and a 7–4 loss to Detroit, but the bigger story is early injury noise down the middle. TribLive reports Ben Kindel and Blake Lizotte issues already stressing center depth, with additional day-to-day tags on Brazeau and Koivunen. Fans tracking the Penguins’ runway into the regular season will want every update from camp medicals.

stories.headline: Connecticut Renaissance Faire heads into Faerie Ring Revels weekend (Sept 26–27)
stories.summary: The Connecticut Renaissance Faire in Lebanon continues its 2026 season with Faerie Ring Revels on September 26–27, featuring fairy and flora costume contests after Shirefolk Weekend. The faire runs on select weekends through late October. For anyone mapping a New England autumn outing with jousts, crafts, and themed weekends, this is the near-term date to circle.

stories.headline: Adirondacks travel pitch: peak foliage paired with family adventure
stories.summary: As September tips into foliage season, the Adirondacks are getting fresh national travel ink for combining early color with family-friendly outdoor itineraries. Guides emphasize shoulder-season pacing — cooler hikes, lake towns, and fewer midsummer crowds than peak July. Elsewhere, fall destination marketing is pushing Smokies and Great Lakes alternatives alongside classic New England leaf-peeping.

stories.headline: Westport Volunteer EMS recruiting for EMT course — life-saving skills for Fairfield County
stories.summary: Westport Volunteer EMS continues its long local tradition of training community EMTs, with coursework covering bandaging, childbirth, and multi-system trauma under veteran instructors. Officials say seats fill quickly with adults from across Fairfield County who want to volunteer. The squad’s mix of paid staff, volunteers, and Norwalk Hospital paramedic backup underpins 24/7 coverage for the town.

stories.headline: Karen Woodall clarifies unauthorized article and distances work from PASG framing
stories.summary: On September 11 expert Karen Woodall publicly clarified that an article bearing her name and photo appeared in Contemporary Family Quarterly without her submission or permission. She notes she left the Parental Alienation Study Group in 2019 and no longer uses classic parental-alienation diagnostic frameworks, focusing instead on children’s attachment adaptations and coerced alignment. Her book The Journey of the Alienated Child is slated for Routledge this autumn.
